entities.summary:
Yarim-Lim of Alalakh was a king of Alalakh, son of Hammurabi I of Yamhad, and the founder of the Alalakhite dynasty, which lasted until the Hittite conquest of the city. He was granted Alalakh by his brother Abba-El I of Yamhad and established a cadet branch of the Yamhadite dynasty. Yarim-Lim's reign marked the beginning of a new era in the region, characterized by increased trade and cultural exchange with the Hittites.


Yarim-Lim of Alalakh was a key figure in the ancient Near East, known for his diplomatic efforts and his role in shaping the regional politics of the time. He was a member of the Yamhadite dynasty, which had a significant impact on the development of the region. Yarim-Lim's reign was marked by a series of events that had far-reaching consequences for the region, including the establishment of trade relationships with the Hittites and the development of a new cultural identity.
